thread:
Alex Chen: Heads-up — we're seeing a lot of variant downgrades for free tier in eu-west1. latency spikes when the fallback quantized models are served. noticed this since midnight UTC.
Nina Patel: Ugh. Is that because of quota enforcement kicking in? any waves in the routing decisions? @cj can you pull routing logs?
CJ Morales: grabbing logs now. short summary: 65% of free requests in eu-west1 switched to tiny-quant at request-time due to soft-quota triggers + region capacity pressure.
Tara Singh: do we have an example policy for free vs pro vs ent that the router uses? maybe the policy is too eager to downgrade in the absence of capacity.
CJ Morales: snippet from current routing policy (console export) — note it's simplified:
```yaml
policies:
  tiers:
    free:
      prefer: [standard-8bit, tiny-quant]
      quota_behavior: soft_downgrade
      max_downgrade_latency_ms: 800
    pro:
      prefer: [standard-8bit, standard-4bit]
      quota_behavior: throttle_then_queue
    enterprise:
      prefer: [standard-8bit]
      quota_behavior: strict_reservation
```
Alex Chen: so free has soft_downgrade which basically lets router fallback to quantized variants when quota consumed or pod busy. but our telemetry shows quality-regression alerts rising and also downstream latency variance.
Nina Patel: can we tweak the free policy to prefer local-region standard-8bit over cross-region standard-4bit? perf > quality tradeoff seems inverted now.
Tara Singh: agree. UI-wise, product wants a tiny toggle per-tenant: allow_variant_downgrade: true/false and a slider for max_downgrade_latency. right now it's all-or-nothing per tier.
CJ Morales: telemetry we sent to console: per-tenant downgrade rate, avg latency before/after downgrade, and regen-quality score. here's a quick query I ran against telemetry-store:
```sql
SELECT tier, region, count(*) as requests, sum(downgraded) as downgrades, avg(latency_ms)
FROM router_events
WHERE ts > now() - interval '6 hours'
GROUP BY tier, region
ORDER BY downgrades DESC
```
Alex Chen: Proposal: change free tier policy to: prefer local standard-8bit, allow single-step downgrade to tiny-quant only if latency threshold exceeded AND regen-quality stays above 0.85, plus expose per-tenant override in console. Also enforce hard quota after 5 consecutive downgrades to avoid spiraling.
Nina Patel: SGTM. Need to ensure we can express "consecutive downgrades" in routing policy language though. maybe a short-lived counter in tenant state.
Tara Singh: UX note: console should show a small inline tooltip next to the toggle: "downgrade makes inference cheaper but may reduce output quality" and a link to run a quick eval. also need per-route telemetry charts showing downgrade events as a stacked area.
rollout-bot: Canary deploy started for patch 0.27.3 — routing-policy update branch applied to canary region eu-west1 (10% traffic). Monitor: /dash/routing/canary/eu-west1
CJ Morales: canary telemetry looks promising so far — downgrade rate dropped 42% in the canary window, latency p95 improved by 120ms, no immediate quality regressions in the sample eval set.
Alex Chen: ok let's expand canary to 30% for 2h, then to 100% if no regression. Nina, Tara, add me to the alert for regen-quality drop > 2% in 30m.
Nina Patel: added. will also add an automated rollback if hard quota breach occurs in a tenant during rollout.
Tara Singh: I'll draft the console copy and tooltip. low-friction per-tenant override + explanation, and add the graph for consecutive downgrades.
Alex Chen: thanks folks. follow-ups: 1) CJ to push canary -> 30% 2) Nina to create rollback alert 3) Tara to push UI mocks by EOD.
CJ Morales: on it. will post canary link and updated stats in channel when done. :rocket:
Nina Patel: thanks — will monitor. :eyes:
Tara Singh: mock uploaded to board. small change: call the toggle "allow automated variant downgrade" and the slider "max acceptable downgrade latency (ms)".
Alex Chen: perfect. keeping this thread pinned until full rollout.
